extracted.intended_audience: general U.S. news readers; policymakers and Congressional actors following the Korean crisis
extracted.subtask_short: news coverage of Truman Korea speech
extracted.subtask_description: Contemporary news reporting summarizing President Truman's radio broadcast on the Korean invasion, Congressional and international reactions, and the Administration's proposed economic mobilization measures. Focuses on policy decisions, mobilization authority, and legislative actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act of aggression / violation of the United Nations Charter
rubrics_metrics.description: The attack upon Korea was an outright breach of the peace and a violation of the Charter of the United Nations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page repeatedly calls the invasion 'an act of raw aggression' and says Communist leaders demonstrated contempt for the basic moral principles on which the United Nations is founded; frames such aggression as a direct challenge to free nations and grounds for UN and collective response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security Council response and criteria for UN action
rubrics_metrics.description: The Security Council passed a resolution calling for the invaders of Korea to stop fighting and withdraw and recommended that members of the United Nations help the Republic of Korea repel the attack and restore peace and security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose of Council action is to stop outbreaks of aggression quickly 'before they develop into general conflicts.' The article notes broad international support (52 of 59 members) and highlights the Soviet boycott as a complicating factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. policy posture: avoid war but keep settlement avenues open
rubrics_metrics.description: If Russia's policy is to avoid war, American officials will not close avenues of approach to working out a settlement, provided basic requirements for restoring the security and independence of South Korea are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle conditions diplomatic engagement on meeting 'basic requirements' for South Korean security and independence; it sits alongside readiness to respond militarily if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate military mobilization priorities (Truman's three items)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three things needed immediately: (1) send more men, equipment, and supplies to General MacArthur; (2) build up the U.S. Army, Navy, and Air Force beyond what is needed in Korea; (3) speed up work with other countries to strengthen common defenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Truman authorized increases to forces drawn from volunteers, Selective Service, National Guard and Reserves, and ordered faster procurement of military supplies; estimated additional cost about ten billion dollars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential authority over contracts and allocations (Economic Mobilization Sec.101(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sec. 101(A) authorizes the President to require that contracts which he deems necessary or appropriate to promote the national defense shall be accepted and performed by any person found to be capable of performance, and be given preference over all other contracts; he is further authorized to allocate materials and facilities on such terms as he may deem appropriate to promote the national defense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as part of the Administration's 'limited economic mobilization bill' to ensure prompt and adequate supplies for military and civilian use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laws to guide flow of materials and restrict nonessential uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation that Congress give the Government power to guide the flow of materials into essential uses, to restrict their use for nonessential purposes, and to prevent the accumulation of unnecessary inventories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as necessary to insure prompt and adequate supplies for military and civilian needs during mobilization; part of economic measures described in the presidential message to Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures to prevent inflation: credit and speculation controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt measures to prevent inflation, including authorizing the Government to set limits on installment buying and to curb speculation in agricultural commodities; apply credit restraints in housing and recommend further controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explained as responding to excessive use of credit as a major cause of inflation; paired with other safeguards such as tax increases and potential rationing/price controls if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax increases to finance defense and eliminate profiteering
rubrics_metrics.description: Make substantial increases in taxes to help finance defense needs, with a major aim of eliminating profiteering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Truman said as soon as a balanced and fair tax program can be worked out he will present it to Congress; framed both as financing mobilization and as an anti-inflation/anti-profiteering measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government-backed financial assistance to private industry for defense production
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government should be authorized to provide certain types of financial assistance to private industry to increase defense production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: many industries already at capacity; increases in defense production may require new capacity or financial help to expand plants and output over several years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal penalties for violation of mobilization controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed bills provide criminal penalties up to a year in jail and a fine of $10,000 for violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These penalties accompany proposed priority/allocation and other economic control measures; hearings were scheduled and leadership hoped for rapid passage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority and allocation authority for strategic materials and production
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals include priority and allocation authority for strategic materials and government-backed financing for essential production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduced in both Houses as part of a package (also including curbs on speculation and consumer credit) to ensure resources are directed to defense needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manpower mobilization methods and removal of ceilings
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase in armed forces will come in part from volunteers, in part from Selective Service, and in part from the National Guard and the Reserves; proposals include taking manpower ceilings off the armed forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senate Armed Services leadership indicated the change could be done quickly and the committee would take up the subject without delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-hoarding, price control and rationing conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Hoarding is 'foolish' and selfish; while current supplies are adequate, if prices rise unduly because of excessive buying or speculation, the Government will take action and the President will not hesitate to recommend rationing and price control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Truman urged citizens not to create shortages by hoarding (especially food) and positioned rationing/price controls as contingency measures if market behavior or speculation produce undue price rises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arms aid appropriations and allocation (House bill)
rubrics_metrics.description: House passed an arms aid bill for $1,222,500,000 to strengthen non-Communist nations; authorizes specific sums (e.g., $1,000,900,000 for arming NATO members; $151,500,000 for Greece and Turkey; $75,000,000 for Philippines and Korea and other regional allocations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as acting by a vote of 361 to 1 and as an early legislative step supporting the president's foreign assistance aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle for UN membership decisions amid aggression
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptance of competing claimant governments for China's seat in the United Nations 'is one which must be reached by the United Nations on its merits' and 'should not be dictated by an unlawful aggression or by any other conduct which would subject the United Nations to coercion and duress.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented in Secretary Acheson's reply to Nehru: diplomatic decisions about UN seats should not be influenced or dictated by acts of aggression in Korea.
